issues.legal_issue: A development authority cannot permit commercial or other non-residential use of land designated for residential use unless the governing plan is lawfully amended through the prescribed process.
material_facts: The operative master plan designated the relevant sector for residential use alone.
Residential plots were used for banks and other commercial businesses without specific permission under a finalized plan or other lawful authorization.
A public notice invited suggestions about possible mixed use, but the proposal was never finalized through the statutory process.
The leases also required the premises to be used for residential purposes.
issues.conclusion: Commercial and other non-residential activity in a sector designated for residential use is impermissible, and the authority has no discretion to authorize it contrary to the operative plan. A change of use requires amendment of the relevant plan and, where necessary, other governing instruments through the prescribed legal process.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6(2)(b) and 6(2)(h), 7, 8, 14, 18 and 19 of the U.P. Industrial Area Development Act, 1976, read with Regulations 2, 3–11 of the New Okhla Industrial Development Area (Preparation and Finalization of Plan) Regulations, 1991, and Regulation 3.22 of the 2006 Building Regulations, make the plan and its designated uses binding. An executive or policy decision cannot alter a statutory plan, and the authority must comply with the prescribed amendment process. The Court relied on NOIDA Entrepreneurs Association v. NOIDA, NDMC v. Tanvi Trading, M.C. Mehta v. Union of India, Bangalore Medical Trust v. B.S. Mudappa, S.N. Chandrashekar v. State of Karnataka, Shabi Construction Company v. CIDCO, K.K. Bhalla v. State of M.P., Dr. G.N. Khajuria v. DDA and ITC Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

rule.if: residential_land_use_case and site_designated_residential and nonresidential_commercial_activity and not plan_lawfully_amended

predicates.residential_land_use_case: The proceeding concerns the regulation of land use by a development authority in an area governed by a development plan.
predicates.site_designated_residential: The operative development plan designates the site or sector for residential use.
predicates.nonresidential_commercial_activity: An occupant or lessee uses the residential site for a commercial or other non-residential activity.
predicates.plan_lawfully_amended: The authority has amended the governing plan through the legally prescribed process to allow the activity.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns planned land use, a site is designated residential, commercial or other non-residential activity occurs there, and the plan has not been lawfully amended, that activity is prohibited.

issues.legal_issue: A limited professional office or simple medical clinic may be carried on in a residential premises within the permitted portion of its ground floor.
material_facts: The governing provisions and lease terms contemplated limited professional or clinical use alongside residential use.
The Court considered the position of doctors, lawyers and architects carrying on professional activities from residential premises.
The Court held that such users could use a limited part of the ground floor for a clinic or office.
issues.conclusion: Doctors may use a limited part of the ground floor for a simple clinic, and lawyers and architects may use a limited part of the ground floor for their offices, subject to the governing rules and any charges lawfully determined after a hearing.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the definition of residential use in Regulation 2(1)(k) of the 1991 Regulations alongside the Regulations, the lease terms and the master plan. It also relied on Delhi Pradesh Citizen Council v. Union of India, which issued similar directions concerning professional use in residential premises.

predicates.residential_professional_use_case: The proceeding concerns professional activity carried on in premises designated for residential use.
predicates.professional_user: A doctor, lawyer or architect carries on the activity from the premises.
predicates.activity_is_a_simple_clinic_or_professio: The activity is a simple clinic or professional office rather than a commercial-scale medical facility or other business.
predicates.use_confined_to_a_limited_ground_floor_a: The professional activity is confined to a limited portion of the ground floor of the premises.

issues.definition: A professional user in residential premises may carry on a simple clinic or professional office if the activity is confined to a limited part of the ground floor.

issues.legal_issue: A medical clinic in a residential area cannot operate as a hospital or as a medical and surgical business on a commercial scale.
material_facts: A premises designated for residential use displayed signs for a clinic and medical-surgical centre, had a reception counter, and contained several doctors’ cabins.
A court-appointed commissioner found that most of the ground floor was used for medical activity and part of another floor was used as an office.
The use went beyond a doctor meeting or examining patients in a limited part of a residence.
issues.conclusion: A hospital or medical clinic of this dimension cannot be permitted in a residential area; a doctor may use a permitted part of the premises for consultation or examination, but may not conduct regular medical and surgical activity on a commercial scale there.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the statutory plan and the residential-use definition in Regulation 2(1)(k) of the 1991 Regulations, together with the lease and governing building rules. It distinguished a simple clinic from a hospital or commercial-scale medical and surgical activity.

predicates.residential_medical_use_case: The proceeding concerns medical activity carried on in premises designated for residential use.
predicates.medical_activity_operates_at_commercial_: The premises are used for a substantial medical or surgical operation, such as a hospital or medical centre, rather than occasional professional consultation.
predicates.activity_exceeds_consultation_or_examina: The activity goes beyond a doctor meeting or examining patients in a limited part of the residence.

issues.definition: Commercial-scale medical or surgical activity that exceeds consultation or examination is prohibited in residential premises.

issues.legal_issue: A proposed mixed-use policy and inconsistent enforcement do not create a legitimate expectation or excuse use that violates a binding residential plan.
material_facts: The authority had issued a public notice inviting suggestions on a proposal to permit some mixed use, but the proposal was not finalized in accordance with law.
The occupants relied on the notice, long-standing activity and examples of similar non-residential uses in other residential premises.
The authority’s enforcement had been inconsistent, although it later maintained that commercial activity was impermissible in residential sectors.
issues.conclusion: The proposed notice did not create a legitimate expectation of permission, statutory requirements could not be waived, and inconsistent enforcement did not legalize the unauthorized use. The authority was required to act fairly and apply the law uniformly.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a sector’s use, fixed by the master plan and statutory regulations, cannot be altered administratively or executively; the doctrine of legitimate expectation does not authorize a departure from statutory requirements, and there can be no waiver of those requirements. It also relied on K. Ramadas Shenoy v. Chief Officer, Town Municipal Council, M.I. Builders v. Radhey Shyam Sahu and Virender Gaur v. State of Haryana on the binding effect of planned uses and the Court’s power to intervene against unlawful departures.

rule.if: residential_use_enforcement_case and unauthorized_nonresidential_use and mixed_use_notice_unfinalized and uneven_enforcement_alleged

predicates.residential_use_enforcement_case: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a residential-use designation in a development plan.
predicates.unauthorized_nonresidential_use: An occupant uses residential premises for a non-residential purpose without lawful authorization.
predicates.mixed_use_notice_unfinalized: The authority issued a notice proposing mixed use, but did not finalize the proposal through the legally prescribed process.
predicates.uneven_enforcement_alleged: The occupant alleges that the authority has not taken the same enforcement action against other similar uses.

issues.definition: An unfinalized mixed-use proposal and alleged inconsistent enforcement do not legalize unauthorized non-residential use of residential premises.

issues.legal_issue: Occupants must stop prohibited non-residential activity in residential premises, and continued misuse after the opportunity to comply requires sealing and lease-cancellation action.
material_facts: The authority had issued notices or cancellation orders concerning commercial activities in residential sectors.
The Court identified banks, nursing homes and other commercial activities operating in residential sectors and directed them to stop the misuse and shift to appropriate areas.
The Court provided an opportunity to comply and directed the authority to seal premises and proceed with lease cancellation if the prohibited activity continued.
issues.conclusion: The prohibited activity must stop and the premises must be restored to residential use. If the lessee or occupant does not stop the misuse within the compliance opportunity, the authority must seal the premises and proceed with lease cancellation; cancellation orders were to remain in abeyance during that opportunity and would be revived if misuse continued, while they would be quashed if misuse was completely stopped.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8 and 14 of the U.P. Industrial Area Development Act, 1976, the lease terms and the binding development plan authorize enforcement against breaches of the designated use. The Court directed that enforcement decisions be made after an opportunity to be heard and that the authority apply the governing law fairly and uniformly.

predicates.residential_misuse_enforcement_case: The proceeding concerns enforcement against non-residential use of premises designated for residential use.
predicates.prohibited_nonresidential_use_continues_: The lessee or occupant continues the prohibited activity after being given an opportunity to stop it.

issues.definition: When prohibited non-residential use continues after an opportunity to comply, the authority must seal the premises and proceed with lease cancellation.
